heard: A giant moon of Saturn vanished every time it orbited east. In 1671, astronomer Giovanni Domenico Cassini tracked Ipetis on Saturn's western side, but lost it entirely on the east. Cassini deduced that Ipetis was tidally locked, with one bright hemisphere and one dark hemisphere. Modern spacecraft proved him right. Its trailing side gleams bright ice, while its leading face is coal black. Because Ipadis takes 79 days to rotate, thermal runaway strips ice into colder zones, leaving dark soot just one foot thick. Then, in 2004, the Cassini probe revealed an equatorial mountain ridge, towering 12 miles high. This colossal mountain wall and bulging waistline give the two-toned moon the bizarre shape of a walnut. How would you explain a world that goes completely invisible on one side of its orbit?
